$comment: Per-engine provisioning facts, so ONE parameterised script can do what five hand-written
Postgres branches do today. This is the data behind DockerEngineProfile.java.draft and
WHY A DESCRIPTOR AND NOT THREE MORE BRANCHES: OperationalRunbookEmitter already carries five
`if ($plan.engine -eq 'Postgres')` blocks. Copying them per engine means 15 blocks across five
user-facing scripts, drifting apart -- the same trap the *-postgres adapters set for the
dialect work, and the reason SqlDialect parameterises twelve methods instead of duplicating
Every 'quirk' below is a MEASURED failure from this project's own CI, not folklore.

Postgres.imageDigestPinned: REQUIRED -- see STOR-3 item 1; a moving tag makes a gate unreadable

listExec: select datname from pg_database order by datname;

createExec: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `{database}` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

quirks: extraRunArgs is NOT optional. MySQL's legacy three-byte 'utf8' cannot represent anything outside the BMP and truncates or replaces it SILENTLY -- the insert succeeds and the data is already wrong. Conformance J2 exists for exactly this.
DDL commits implicitly: a failed multi-step migration leaves earlier steps applied. See STOR-2 and the E6 vector.
A TEXT column cannot be indexed without a key length (error 1170). NPDev's own npdev_flow_instances hit this -- see STOR-4.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS are NOT supported (error 1064). CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is. See STOR-5.

SqlServer.imageDigestPinned: REQUIRED -- and beware: MCR once served a schema-1 prettyjws manifest whose digest was real, stable, and refused by modern Docker. Pin a digest you have actually pulled.

listExec: SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT name FROM sys.databases
createExec: IF DB_ID('{database}') IS NULL CREATE DATABASE [{database}]

quirks: createsDatabaseFromEnv is FALSE. There is no MSSQL_DATABASE variable -- the database must be created after the container is healthy, or the app connects to a database that does not exist.
The SA password must satisfy the strong-password policy. A weak one makes the container EXIT during startup, which surfaces downstream as 'connection refused' and reads like a networking fault.
Startup is slow -- 30-60s is normal. A readiness probe with a Postgres-sized timeout will report a healthy engine as broken.
The username is always 'sa' for the container; a per-app username is a database user created afterwards, not a container env var.
VARCHAR is single-byte and mangles non-ASCII; NVARCHAR is required. portableColumnType() already maps this -- see the J1/J2 vectors.
No guarded-DDL idiom is supported: CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS all need IF OBJECT_ID(...)/IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT ... FROM sys.*) wrappers. See STOR-5.
rowLimit() throws today: SQL Server has no suffix row cap, TOP is a prefix.
No container. Create-Environment only has to ensure the data directory exists.
This is why the parity gate exempts embedded engines from the container operations -- an embedded engine legitimately differs, and pretending otherwise would be its own dishonesty.
Started as a java process, not a container: org.h2.tools.Server -tcp.

TODAY THIS IS BROKEN FOR EVERY USER BUT THE AUTHOR: the emitted Create-Environment.ps1 searches 'D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build' for the H2 jar (OperationalRunbookEmitter line 193, and the same path in its error message at 196). REG-144's family, shipped inside the user's own app. Resolve the jar relative to the app, or from the runtimehost-libs directory the app already knows.
No physical database at all. Every environment operation is a no-op that must SAY it is a no-op rather than printing nothing.

userFacingOperations.$comment: The five things a user does. Parity means all five behave the same way for every server engine -- see PARITY_MATRIX.md.
userFacingOperations.create: Create-Environment.ps1  -- start the engine, wait for ready, ensure the database exists
userFacingOperations.stop: Stop-Environment.ps1    -- stop the engine, leave the data
userFacingOperations.status: Show-Environment.ps1  -- is it running, on what port, with what data
userFacingOperations.connect: Show-DbConnection.ps1 -- the details to paste into a DB GUI
userFacingOperations.reset: Reset-Environment.ps1  -- stop, remove, delete the data
